author: BoldAndBrash
body:
There has been lots of talk about this. People saying they've been falsely banned for hacking, advertising, innaprop. links, and much more. I decided to create a new topic to make sure many people see it. 

Many players including me have been given infractions we don't believe in. Someone I know got an infraction for saying "I fisted you to death" and I guess the person worded that kinda bad. But no verbal warning, just /warn. Plus, she was telling the Staff member it was all a misunderstanding and he wouldn't even reply.

I believe Staff members should begin recording/screenshotting rule breakers. It will help out a lot because now whenever a player says it was false they either get ignored or just laughed at. This will also help a lot with people who actually DID hack and decide to make a topic on the forums. The mod could send a link then lock the topic.

And yes, I understand having 100 of videos may be bad for your computer, but you can just delete them after you're done using them.


Please do NOT take this as a "hate" topic. This is constructive criticism. So far, I believe the Staff team is doing a decent job. Thanks for reading, and I hope this begins to happen!

replies.author: Porkyyy
replies.body:
When we see someone spamming or being rude in-game, we /warn or /kick.
When the come back and act the same again, that is when we tempban. We don't necessarily always check the players' infractions to see if he already has x number of infractions regarding the same thing.
However if a player has 2 or more pages of infractions, we tempban them for Excessive Infractions.
In the end, they will get tempbanned / banned for it anyways.

replies.author: TheTNTPotato
replies.body:
Only rant to Sr Staff+* (I promise I'm joking)

When you question the decision and bash the moderator about it, you're essentially humiliating them. If they've done something wrong, PM them saying how they can improve.

There is a difference between helping a staff member improve, and publicly (heck, even privately in the Slack is a little embarrassing) calling them out on the mistake. If they disagree with what you say, that is fine too, but make sure that your suggestion for improvement will actually help them.
